summary: Plan community health interventions, apply COM-B and evaluate outcomes. Explore the health promotion course and its practical curriculum.
lede: Health promotion training helps public health practitioners, community educators and programme coordinators turn community needs into practical interventions. Participants assess needs, analyse behaviour with COM-B and design audience-specific health communication and activities. They also map partners, set indicators and draft evaluation plans and progress reports, drawing on the Ottawa Charter and PRECEDE-PROCEED to connect evidence with programme decisions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who plan, deliver, coordinate or evaluate health promotion and community health activities. It suits practitioners who need to turn community evidence into workable interventions, coordinate delivery partners and report progress clearly.
modules: Ottawa Charter and Health Promotion Practice
prerequisites: The supplied course information does not specify entry prerequisites. Familiarity with community health, public health programmes or health education work will help you apply the exercises; prior study of the named frameworks is not required by the course outline. Coding is not required. Advanced evaluation approaches are introduced conceptually, while programme planning and indicator exercises focus on operational application.
